name: Motorscooter
description: A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an automatic transmission whose electric motor is rated at no more than 5,000 watts, on a wheelbase of 64 inches or less and weighing no more than 450 pounds dry. An electric two-wheeler that tops an electric bicycle's 750 watts or 28 mph, or lacks operable pedals, lands here while it stays within these limits. Defined by Tennessee Code Annotated §55-8-101.
restrictions: Two or three wheels and an automatic transmission
An electric motor of no more than 5,000 watts (or a 300 cc, 30 horsepower combustion engine), a wheelbase of no more than 64 inches and a dry weight of no more than 450 pounds
No top-speed limit in the definition
Riders need a Class M or Class M-limited license; the Department of Safety issues the limited license from 16, or from 15 restricted to 4 a.m. to 8 p.m. within seven miles of home
Riders and passengers must wear a crash helmet, one meeting FMVSS 218 if under 21
Titled and registered as a motor vehicle
One over 5,000 watts, 450 pounds or a 64-inch wheelbase, or with a manual transmission, is a motorcycle
